knowledge_point.title: Calculating the Vertical Asymptotes of a Rational Function

question.:question/problem: Calculate the vertical asymptotes of $f(x) = \frac{2}{2 - x} + \frac{3}{2 + x}$.
question.:question/worked-solution:
To find the vertical asymptotes of a rational function, we factor the numerator and denominator and cancel any common factors. Then, we set the denominator equal to zero and solve for $x.$

Adding both fractions and then factoring the numerator and denominator, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & =\frac{2}{2-x}+\frac{3}{2+x} \\ & =\frac{2(2+x)+3(2-x)}{(2-x)(2+x)} \\ & =\frac{4+2x+6-3x}{(2-x)(2+x)} \\ & =\frac{10-x}{(2-x)(2+x)}.\end{aligned}
$$

There are no common factors in the numerator and denominator, so we set the denominator equal to zero and solve for $x:$

$$
(2-x)(2+x)=0
$$

This gives the two solutions $x=-2$ and $x=2$. 

Therefore, the equations of the vertical asymptotes are $x=-2$ and $x=2$.

Adding both fractions and then factoring the numerator and denominator, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & =\frac{3}{x + 1}+\frac{4}{x - 7} \\  & =\frac{3(x - 7)+4(x + 1)}{(x + 1)(x - 7)} \\  & =\frac{3 x-21+4 x+4}{(x + 1)(x - 7)} \\  & =\frac{7 x - 17}{(x + 1)(x - 7)}.\end{aligned}
$$

There are no common factors in the numerator and denominator, so we set the denominator equal to zero and solve for $x:$

$$
(x + 1)(x - 7)=0
$$

This gives the two solutions $x=-1$ and $x=7$. 

Therefore, the equations of the vertical asymptotes are $x=-1$ and $x=7$.
